text.tspan: Page 13, How to read this book
What the pen says, word for word, and what it means
FACT OR OPINION, VISIBLY
“there is data to support this: that paper &
book reading is better to learn”
Read on paper is backed by data: find it and cite it,
instead of 'my experience rather than a finding'.
WHAT WORKS, KEEP IT
“✓ [beside: Read it somewhere you can give
it your undivided attention.]”
Keep.
THE VOICE IS MINE
“Reword from an 'adult first' [?] approach”
Reword the reading path; the key word is uncertain ('adult
first'?), for Dinis to confirm.
MEET THE READER WHERE THEY ARE
“that is not our recommendation, I think
[under: so do not skip them.]”
The book should not tell founders they must not skip
chapters.
THE VOICE IS MINE
“not anymore :) [over: says developer]”
The title says founders now (decision 019).
SHOW THE BOOK, DO NOT LIST IT
“Brian May story, Queen [beside: because the
tools can be made to fit you]”
Craftspeople made their own tools: tell the story of Brian
May, of Queen, who built his own guitar.
WHAT WORKS, KEEP IT
“✓ [beside: You are lucky to be here. Not
because it will be easy ...]”
Keep the closing line.
MEET THE READER WHERE THEY ARE
“Actually I think we should expand &
recommend here the workflow that I (right
now) am having with you (Claude) where you
are understanding & capturing my ideas as I
read this RC & is something that I want to
start doing the next time I read a book”
How to read this book should recommend this workflow: read
on paper with a pen, photograph the pages, and let an
agent capture the notes.
